nodes.under_the_hood: Static application entry point. It loads styles.css and tailwind.css, includes the Cloudflare Turnstile script for bot protection, then defers api.js, db.js, sync.js, vocab.js, scoring.js, and app.js in that dependency order. api.js is first because it publishes window.SevApi.BASE, which vocab.js reads while building its config. All local asset URLs use the v2.3.0 cache key, and the page registers sw.js after load.

Primary UI and route orchestrator. It hydrates question-bank data from IndexedDB, renders the SPA shell and SAT practice flows (including tracking omitted custom test responses, option toggling, and RW passage text highlighting with boundary clamping, as well as the Mistakes Log), and owns onboarding, history, backup, tutorial, and hash/popstate routing. Vocabulary is an independent route: an active window.Vocab session restores #vocab on startup, bypasses question-bank onboarding, and counts as restorable data when a returning account is synced. app.js exposes window.renderHome so vocab.js can request a UI refresh. It also conditionally loads PostHog and Sentry upon telemetry consent: PostHog with autocapture, pageviews, dead clicks, surveys, heatmaps, feature flags and session recording all disabled and a property denylist covering question text and answers, and Sentry with browser tracing sampled at 0.1 and no Session Replay integration. It also owns the client half of the shared question catalog: normalizing downloaded payloads into IndexedDB (dropping the self-referential `raw` field, which would otherwise double what is stored), retiring banks the download emptied, resuming an interrupted download at boot and after a backup restore, and excluding catalog questions from exports and backups via buildPortablePayload(). renderHome() forces the onboarding view whenever no questions are stored, so a finished catalog download has to move the view off it explicitly -- guarded on the current view, because an existing user can sit on onboarding deliberately to import another file. The feedback modal keeps a failed submission on screen with the server's own reason (a 4xx message verbatim, a quotable status code for a 5xx) instead of hiding the form behind a generic connection error and discarding the draft on a timer.

Single source of truth for the Cloudflare Worker origin, published as window.SevApi and loaded before every other script. Owns the catalog download driver: meta, Turnstile-backed ticket, keyset paging, retry with backoff, ticket re-minting when a long download outlives a 10-minute ticket, restart on a mid-download version change, and a resume cursor persisted to appConfig after every page. The caller injects the `store` callback, because normalizing a question and writing it to IndexedDB needs app.js internals that do not belong here.

IndexedDB wrapper exposed as window.SatPracticeDB. It provides promise-based get, getAll, put, putMany, remove, and clear operations for questionBanks, questions, sessions, responses, appConfig, and vocabWords. The appConfig store additionally holds the catalog download cursor under the key "questionCatalog", persisted after every page so an interrupted download costs at most one page.
Dedicated Web Worker for running background IndexedDB data migrations and legacy encryption conversions without blocking the main UI thread.

Pure deterministic scoring engine providing Student-Produced Response (SPR) sanitization, math expression/fraction normalization, and MCQ/SPR answer grading shared across the main thread and background workers.

Vocabulary SRS module. It seeds vocabWords from dsat_vocabulary.json, manages learn and flashcard sessions, and persists resumable session state in localStorage under sat_vocab_state. It exposes isSessionActive(), reloadState(), and rendering/session methods through window.Vocab. Progress updates are written to IndexedDB and optionally synced through SevSync. Includes dynamic Cloudflare Turnstile integration with safe unmounting and offscreen positioning to avoid display-none throttling while securing AI sentence validation endpoints.

Optional Google Drive appData sync module exposed as window.SevSync. It stores link metadata and short-lived access tokens in localStorage, merges local and remote records with last-write-wins rules, and syncs both vocabWords and sat_vocab_state. Background syncing runs only with a valid cached token; manual sync renews the Google session when needed.

Dedicated Web Worker for off-thread Google Drive remote data diffing, delta merging, and storage synchronization. Shared-catalog questions are stripped from both sides of the merge: they are re-downloadable from the worker, so keeping them out of the Drive blob is what takes a synced account from roughly 47 MB down to a few hundred KB. Stripping only the local side would make every remote copy look like a missing record and write the whole bank back into IndexedDB under its old bank id, so remote copies are matched by bank id *and* by the local catalog id set -- a blob written before the download carries the same questions under the original import's bank id. A blob that still holds them forces exactly one rewrite even when nothing else changed.

Network-first service worker with cache fallback for GET requests. It precaches the v2.3.0 application asset set in sat-practice-cache-v2.3.0, bypasses the browser HTTP cache during install, activates immediately, and deletes older named caches. Every worker script that importScripts or `new Worker()`s another file pins the same v2.3.0 key, so a version bump has to be applied together across index.html, sw.js (both CACHE_NAME and the precache list), db.js, db-worker.js, sync.js, sync-worker.js, privacy.html and APP_VERSION in app.js -- a file that asks for an older key is not in the new cache and fails offline. One bump per release, not per commit.
Hand-authored responsive application styles, including the sidebar, modals, loading states, SAT practice UI, and vocabulary session/flashcard layouts.
Committed, precompiled Tailwind utility stylesheet used alongside styles.css.
Static vocabulary seed data fetched by vocab.js when the vocabWords store is empty.

Cloudflare Worker HTTP entry point. Routing happens before method dispatch, so the GET banner is a fallback rather than a short-circuit that would shadow every catalog route. Owns the per-route rate-limit map, the X-Admin-Key check scoped to /api/admin/*, and the deliberate rule that a valid admin key also satisfies the download-ticket gate and exempts the caller from rate limits -- which is what lets tools/upload_catalog.py --verify read pages back through the real public route. Page requests get a deliberately generous budget because the ticket, not the page route, is the per-person cost gate: a tight page budget would not stop scraping but would break a computer lab whose 20 simultaneous downloads arrive from one NAT address.

Shared HTTP helpers for the worker: a CORS origin allowlist (GitHub Pages, localhost, plus an optional ALLOWED_ORIGINS var) that emits Vary: Origin and no ACAO header at all for disallowed origins, a JSON response helper, integer parameter clamping, and base64url codecs.

The endpoints that shipped before the catalog: consent acknowledgement, the Discord feedback relay, and Gemini-backed vocabulary sentence validation. Also exports the shared verifyTurnstile() used by the catalog ticket route, which enforces the token's `action` so a token minted for one endpoint cannot be replayed against another. WORKER_API_KEY is scoped to this handler rather than global. The evaluator model comes from the GEMINI_MODEL var and the hardcoded fallback must name the same model: they once disagreed, so a deploy that did not supply the var silently moved production onto a retired model and every sentence check fell back to the client's heuristic path. The feedback relay caps attachments at five and returns 400 for a missing message, so those are the client-visible cases; a missing DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL surfaces as a 500 rather than a silent success.

Read-only question catalog served out of D1 plus the admin ingestion routes. The read path never JSON.parses or JSON.stringifies a question payload -- a worker gets 10 ms of CPU per request, and re-serializing a 1 MB page would spend it all -- so a page body is assembled by concatenating D1's already-string payloads inside a hand-written envelope. Pagination is keyset over a contiguous seq column with an inclusive `since` cursor. Downloads are gated by an HMAC-SHA256 ticket that is bound to the catalog version and expires in 10 minutes; a version mismatch answers 409 so the client restarts rather than treating it as an auth failure. Whether the gate applies is declared in wrangler.toml rather than inferred from whether the secret exists, so a forgotten secret surfaces as a 503 instead of a silently ungated catalog. Missing tables read as an empty catalog so a created-but-uninitialised database does not answer 500.

Worker deployment config. Staging is the default environment so a bare `wrangler deploy` cannot reach production, which is deployed explicitly with --env production. Named environments inherit nothing, so vars, the D1 binding and every secret are repeated per environment and `wrangler secret put` without --env sets the secret on staging only. Staging and production bind separate databases -- sevrony-questions-staging and sevrony-questions -- so a bad upload or a --reset aimed at the wrong target cannot touch the catalog real users download. Lists every secret the operator must set with `wrangler secret put` -- ADMIN_KEY, CATALOG_TICKET_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET, GEMINI_API_KEY, DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL -- none of which are ever committed or exposed to the frontend, and ADMIN_KEY deliberately differs between environments so a staging leak grants no write access to the live catalog. GEMINI_MODEL is a var rather than a secret and has to match the fallback in worker/vocab.js.

Cloudflare D1 database holding the shared read-only question bank: a `questions` table keyed by College Board external id with a contiguous seq column for keyset pagination and the question JSON in a `payload` column, plus a `catalog_meta` key/value table carrying the version string and counts. Keying on the College Board id is what makes the switch from a hand-imported bank lossless: responses join questions by questionId, so answers and study state carry over even though the bank id changes. Sized well inside the free tier's 500 MB per database and 2 MB per row. Exists twice -- sevrony-questions for production and sevrony-questions-staging -- both serving the same catalog version built from one .sat-test export. The admin ingestion path creates its own schema, so a freshly created empty database needs no separate migration step and reads as an empty catalog (503) rather than a 500 until the first upload lands.
PWA manifest defining the install name, colors, display mode, start URL, and logo icons.
Primary application and PWA icon, referenced by the page, manifest, and service-worker cache list.

Operator and test tooling, not shipped to the browser. build_catalog_db.py turns a .sat-test export into catalog.sqlite (gitignored, ~23 MB). upload_catalog.py pushes it to the worker in 25-row batches, taking the admin key from an env var, a file or a prompt but never from argv, where it would land in shell history and ps output; it writes catalog_meta last so an interrupted upload leaves the old version string describing a complete catalog, and --verify walks every page back through the real public route. test_worker.mjs, test_catalog_client.mjs and test_sync_catalog.mjs run the worker, the download driver and the sync filter offline against the real catalog using node:sqlite as a D1 shim, with Turnstile, Discord and Gemini replaced by a recording fetch stub so the feedback relay and the evaluator's model choice are asserted without network. Coverage exists for the routes that had none and broke in production: the feedback relay and the GEMINI_MODEL fallback.
